descriptors.R: nominee of the party that held the presidency from 1953 to 1961
descriptors.D: nominee of the party of the administration in office since 1961, which also holds majorities in both houses of Congress

compile_desc.R: the party that held the presidency from 1953 to 1961
compile_desc.D: the party of the administration in office since 1961, which also holds majorities in both houses of Congress

others_line: Other choices on some ballots, including an unpledged elector slate in Alabama and Socialist Labor and Socialist Workers nominees (answer "other").
never_name: Johnson, Goldwater, Humphrey, Miller, Kennedy, Rockefeller, Scranton, Lodge, Wallace, Nixon or Eisenhower

slice_sources.men: 1960 and 1970 censuses interpolated to November 1964; men 21+ (18+ in Georgia and Kentucky, 19+ in Alaska, 20+ in Hawaii) outside the eleven Southern states, in the 50 states and DC (first presidential vote in DC, Twenty-third Amendment); calibrated to certified 1964 returns.
slice_sources.women: 1960 and 1970 censuses interpolated to November 1964; women 21+ (18+ in Georgia and Kentucky, 19+ in Alaska, 20+ in Hawaii) outside the eleven Southern states, in the 50 states and DC (first presidential vote in DC, Twenty-third Amendment); calibrated to certified 1964 returns.
slice_sources.south-white: 1960 and 1970 censuses interpolated to November 1964; white adults (21+ (18+ in Georgia and Kentucky, 19+ in Alaska, 20+ in Hawaii)) in the eleven former Confederate states (includes a small number of American Indian and Asian adults) (the Twenty-fourth Amendment ended poll taxes in federal elections in January 1964); calibrated to certified 1964 returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1960 and 1970 censuses interpolated to November 1964; Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states; registration still held to well under half of Black adults by literacy tests, registrar discretion and intimidation (the Voting Rights Act came only in 1965). The shortfall against white turnout is counted as exclusion.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1960 and 1970 censuses interpolated to November 1964; foreign-born white adults who were not naturalized citizens (aliens could not vote in any state).

masks: the nominee of the party out of power
a rival for the nomination of the party out of power
